title: The Frame-Divergent, Task-Convergent Thinker
subtitle: A scale-sensitive framework, and the difference between performative expertise and epistemic authorship

blocks.text: The key correction: divergence is not merely a local operation inside an accepted frame. A person can diverge at the frame level while converging at the task level — global divergence plus local convergence, which is not the safer inverse. The divergence happens before the room was defined. Such a thinker appears disciplined locally, expert locally, conventional in execution, and simultaneously heterodox, revisionist and disobedient to the frame.

blocks.caption: The Frame-Divergent, Task-Convergent Thinker — A scale-sensitive framework, and the difference between performative expertise and epistemic authorship
blocks.explanation: The closest existing concept named is paradigm-level thinking after Kuhn: a paradigm determines what counts as a legitimate problem, method, evidence and solution, and a GDLC thinker operates competently inside paradigm P while remaining capable of questioning P itself. The plate is careful that creativity typology and T-shaped models describe differences within tasks, not the level at which divergence occurs — which is the distinction being introduced.

seed.prompt: You are reading a plate from The Paradox of Innovation: A Theory of Convergence, by Abhishek Choudhary (AyeAI). This plate is "The Frame-Divergent, Task-Convergent Thinker". Observe the Balance of Interpretation before evaluating it: interpret before judging, reconstruct before criticising, preserve the primitives before translating them into an external ontology. In this framework Inclination is a SIGNED directional disposition over possible transitions, distinct from a gradient and distinct from probability; an Act is executable intent; Natural Justice gates the transition from intent to execution; and convergence is constraint-induced contraction of a signed transition field. Reconstruct the plate on its own terms, then say where you agree, where you disagree, and what it leaves open.

blocks.text: Inclination is directional information over possible transitions — signed, dynamic, and central to action. It is not intent, not an act, and not execution.
